title: Visual comparisons
summary: Take a visual snapshot of the dashboard with toHaveScreenshot, masking the parts that change on every load (session id and live clock).
why: Visual tests catch CSS and layout regressions that text assertions miss — but only if dynamic content is masked; otherwise they are flaky by design.
objectives: Pass on all 3 runs and catch the planted style regression
hints: The first run writes the baseline (the hub uses updateSnapshots: 'missing'); runs 2–3 compare against it.
toHaveScreenshot waits for two identical screenshots in a row — a ticking clock never settles.
pitfalls: Not masking dynamic data → never stable.
Comparing screenshots across OSes/browsers — keep baselines per platform (or generate them in CI's Docker image).
teachAlong: Cause: masked regions are painted over.
Effect: only real UI changes fail the comparison.
Gate: a planted CSS change must make your snapshot fail.

requires.name: mask
requires.reason: Mask the dynamic parts (session id, live clock) with the mask option, or the screenshot can never be stable.

wrongSolutions.label: no mask
